QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_25

question.text: Nari Shakti Trust has formed 200 Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in Odisha; 120 women have started micro-enterprises. Odisha's Mission Shakti scheme also trains SHG members and subsidises micro-credit. Under SAS-400, how should the SIA handle attribution?

answer.text: Claim 100% of enterprise formation as Nari Shakti's attributable impact
Drop the indicator since attribution is impossible
Design a comparison between Mission-Shakti-only villages and Mission-Shakti-plus-Nari-Shakti villages (quasi-experimental difference), disclose both contribution and NET attribution

explanation.text: The Logic: SAS-400 gender attribution under a co-funding scenario requires a quasi-experimental design — compare treatment (both schemes) vs control (scheme-only) villages and difference-in-differences the outcome. This is the structure that isolates Nari Shakti's NET contribution. Option C captures this cleanly. The Trap: Option A over-claims. Option B concedes too easily — a comparison design is usually feasible. Option D is non-serious but represents the 'just pick something' temptation. Cross-Exam Context: Same quasi-experimental logic in XV (Research Analyst — event-study design) and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — impact-advice attribution). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Before the engagement starts, ask the SE to identify 3 'control villages' where the SE is NOT active but the government scheme is. This makes your attribution defensible without a full RCT.
